name: Steenkamp Dilation Versus Urethrotomy Trial
question: Does optical internal urethrotomy reduce stricture recurrence compared with filiform dilation as outpatient treatment for male urethral stricture?

design.population: 210 men with proven urethral stricture treated as outpatients under local anesthesia in Stellenbosch, South Africa, enrolled January 1991 to January 1994.
design.description: Single-center randomized comparison of two outpatient endoscopic treatments
design.locator: Abstract (1997 report: n=210, 106 and 104); 1998 abstract (enrollment dates)

verdictNote: Recurrence did not differ between dilation and urethrotomy; stricture length predicted failure.
takeaway: In 210 men randomized to optical internal urethrotomy (104) or filiform dilation (106) as outpatient treatment for urethral stricture, recurrence-free survival did not differ significantly; recurrence risk rose with stricture length (hazard ratio 1.22 per centimeter, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.43).

reports.label: Initial report
reports.citation: Steenkamp JW, Heyns CF, de Kock ML. Internal urethrotomy versus dilation as treatment for male urethral strictures: a prospective, randomized comparison. *J Urol.* 1997;157(1):98-101.

results.measure: Stricture recurrence by life-table survival analysis, urethrotomy versus dilation
results.note: No significant difference between the two treatments; arm-specific rates are not reported in the abstract.

results.measure: Hazard function of recurrence over time (both treatments)
results.note: Risk of recurrence was greatest at 6 months; risk of failure after 12 months was slight.

results.endpoint: Recurrence by stricture length: shorter than 2 cm
results.measure: Recurrence at 12 months, strictures shorter than 2 cm (both treatments)

results.endpoint: Recurrence by stricture length: 2 to 4 cm
results.measure: Recurrence at 12 and 48 months, strictures 2 to 4 cm (both treatments)
results.note: Approximately 50% at 12 months, rising to approximately 75% at 48 months.

results.endpoint: Recurrence by stricture length: longer than 4 cm
results.measure: Recurrence at 12 months, strictures longer than 4 cm (both treatments)
Hazard of recurrence per 1 cm increase in stricture length, Cox regression

reports.label: Procedure complications and failure
reports.dateLocator: PubMed: S Afr J Surg 1997 Aug;35(3)
reports.citation: Steenkamp JW, Heyns CF, de Kock ML. Outpatient treatment for male urethral strictures: dilatation versus internal urethrotomy. *S Afr J Surg.* 1997;35(3):125-130.
reports.noDoi: No DOI is registered for this South African Journal of Surgery article.

results.measure: Cumulative percentage of recurrent strictures, urethrotomy versus dilation
results.note: No significant difference between the two treatments at mean follow-up of 15 months.

harms.label: Complications or failure during the procedure
harms.note: No significant difference between dilation and urethrotomy. For dilation, more frequent with presentation as retention or complications than with symptoms only, and with a positive than a negative urine culture. For urethrotomy, more frequent with a positive urine culture and with strictures longer than 2 cm than shorter than 2 cm (multiple strictures, P = 0.06).

harms.label: Failure of urethrotomy alone
harms.note: More frequent with post-traumatic than post-urethritic strictures and in men without previous stricture treatment.

reports.label: Repeated-treatment analysis
reports.citation: Heyns CF, Steenkamp JW, De Kock ML, Whitaker P. Treatment of male urethral strictures: is repeated dilation or internal urethrotomy useful? *J Urol.* 1998;160(2):356-358.
reports.followUp: Mean 24 months (range 2 to 63) in 163 of 210 patients (78%)

results.measure: Stricture-free rate at 24 and 48 months after one dilation or urethrotomy with no recurrence at 3 months
results.note: Among 73 of 107 men at risk (68%) who were stricture-free at 3 months after one study procedure, estimated stricture-free survival was about 60% at 24 and 48 months in the analysis including men with and without previous treatment (Fig. 2); alternate analyses yielded 55 to 60% at 24 months and 50 to 60% at 48 months (Figs. 3–4).

results.endpoint: Stricture-free rate after a second procedure
results.measure: Stricture-free rate at 24 and 48 months after a second dilation or urethrotomy for recurrence at 3 months
results.note: After a second study procedure for recurrence at 3 months, estimated stricture-free survival was about 30% at 24 months and 0% at 48 months in the analysis including men with and without previous treatment (Fig. 2), and about 40% and 0% among men without previous treatment (Fig. 3); in Fig. 4, which counts pre-study treatment as the first treatment, the estimates after a second treatment were about 50% at 24 months and 40% at 48 months, and 0% at both time points after a third.

results.endpoint: Stricture-free rate after a third procedure
results.measure: Stricture-free rate at 24 months after a third dilation or urethrotomy for recurrence at 3 and 6 months
results.note: 0% at 24 months; p < 0.0001 compares the one-, two-, and three-procedure strata, with survival measured from the last treatment.

delivery.label: Repeat procedures
delivery.value: Dilation or urethrotomy repeated at the first and second stricture recurrence
